full-population.t: Here are **100 emails**. Pick one at random. Every email is equally likely to be the one you get, so **all 100 are in play**.

event-a.h: EVENT A: THE EMAIL IS SPAM
event-a.t: **40 of the 100** emails are spam (pink). So **P(spam) = 40 / 100 = 0.4**. This is the probability before we know anything else.

observe-b.t: Now you learn that the email contains the word **“free”**. **30 of the 100** emails contain it. We are being told the email is one of these 30.

restrict-to-b.t: Everything outside the dashed box is **ruled out**. The universe we pick from shrank from **100 emails to 30**. That is the heart of conditioning.

overlap.t: Inside the 30 “free” emails, **24 are spam** (bright pink) and **6 are not**. The overlap of A and B is 24 emails.

conditional-ratio.t: **P(spam | free) = P(spam and free) / P(free) = 24/100 ÷ 30/100 = 24 / 30 = 0.8.** The denominator changed from 100 to 30.

ml-connection.t: Before seeing the word, spam had probability **0.4**. Given “free”, it is **0.8**. A classifier makes every prediction this way: **conditioned on the evidence it can see**.
